data.narrative:
Nuvacore is a Seed-stage semiconductor company founded by Gerard Williams III, John Bruno, and Ram Srinivasan. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 11 private peers and 3 public comparables in the Chips & Semiconductors sector, including Series A companies SambaNova Systems, Rebellions, and d-Matrix.

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach. Three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private peers yield a median valuation of $2.3B, with a range spanning $2.0B (d-Matrix) to $11.0B (SambaNova Systems). Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples cannot be applied without Nuvacore's revenue data, which remains undisclosed. The semiconductor sector median P/S across public names (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) stands at 20.5x, but this lacks a denominator for meaningful calibration at the target.

The triangulated range supported by available data is $2.0B to $2.7B, centered on $2.3B. This reflects a narrow evidence base—one applicable method across three peers—and material uncertainty regarding how Nuvacore's technology positioning and capital requirements compare within the peer set. The $11.0B outlier (SambaNova) suggests stage-based variance is meaningful. Key uncertainties include the target's actual development status relative to Series A peers and whether its founders' backgrounds command a premium or discount to peer valuations.
